title: Bitwise operators
description: Bitwise tricks unlock many interview problems — single-number, missing-number, power-of-two — and `~~x` is a fast floor for non-negative numbers.

notes: Bitwise ops coerce numbers to **32-bit signed** integers — fractional parts and values above 2^31 - 1 get truncated/wrapped.
`>>` is the signed (arithmetic) shift — sign bit is preserved. `>>>` is the unsigned (logical) shift and yields a uint32.
`~~x` truncates toward zero (`Math.trunc`), not toward -Infinity. Use it instead of `Math.floor` only when `x >= 0`.

questions.q: Which expression checks whether `n` is odd?
questions.explain: ANDing with 1 isolates the lowest bit.

questions.q: Which operator is the UNSIGNED right shift?
questions.explain: `>>>` zero-fills from the left, yielding a uint32.

questions.q: After `a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b;` starting with `a=5, b=9`, what are `a, b`?
questions.explain: Classic XOR swap — no temp variable needed.

exercises.prompt: XOR-swap two values without a temp.
Test whether the 2nd bit (index 1, value 2) is set in 6.

L3.prompt: Given `[4, 1, 2, 1, 2]` where every element appears twice except one, find the single number using XOR. Log it.
hints: XOR-fold the whole array — duplicates cancel, the loner remains.
